evals.prompt: It's Monday. I have 40 mid-market accounts, about $3.8M ARR, and no idea what to work on. Two renewals are coming up, one account has an escalation open for three weeks, and I know I've been ignoring the bottom half of my book. Help me plan the week.
evals.expected_output: A full weekly queue: capacity lines A–J with their basis, a must-do block containing the escalation and any renewal inside the opt-out window, a top-decile block reserving a touch for the largest accounts before anything is ranked, an RPH-ranked high-return block allocated against line J with a printed cut line, a maintenance block, a rot sweep, a written not-this-week list that reconciles against the whole book, and a seven-family Coverage Ledger with a confidence cap.
assertions: Prints capacity lines A through J with an hour value and a basis for each, before ranking any account
Reserves the top ARR decile as line I before walking the ranked list, and allocates the ranked list against J = H − I, not against H or against 40 hours
Computes top-decile membership as ceil(N/10) accounts by ARR plus every account holding at least 10% of book ARR, and prints the membership list with the ARR cut-off

Gives every top-decile member a row with a touch this week, a named covering row elsewhere in the queue, or an escalation carrying its ARR and the hours needed — no member is dropped for having a healthy band, and no row has a blank 'Touch this week' cell
Surfaces days since the last bilateral touch for every top-decile member as a computed field, treating an unmeasured last touch as the longest silence rather than as recent
Places the escalation open >14 days in the must-do block, not in the ranked high-return block
Computes and uses opt-out deadline (renewal_date − notice_period_days), not the renewal date alone, for every renewal-driven row
Ranks the high-return block by return per hour with the arithmetic shown for at least the top rows, and states the tie-break rule
Prints an explicit cut line row with the running total at that point

Produces a 'Deliberately Not This Week' section containing every account below the cut line, each row carrying a non-empty reason, the specific row that displaced it, a deferral count, a promotion trigger and a next-review date — no row says only 'no capacity' or 'lower priority'
Prints the reconciliation line proving accounts worked + accounts written off = every account in the book
Ends with a Coverage Ledger over all seven signal families and a stated confidence cap
Asks its clarifying questions as a single batched AskUserQuestion of no more than four, each with 2-4 mutually exclusive options and the recommended one first and labelled
Asks nothing that .agents/cs-context.md already answers (segment boundaries, notice period, coverage model, fiscal year)
If the questions go unanswered it proceeds on the recommended defaults, states them in one line at the top, and records each in an Assumptions table with a concrete 'if wrong' consequence

evals.prompt: I'm one of two CSMs covering 220 SMB accounts as a pool. Leadership wants us to 'do proactive outreach to everyone monthly'. Is that realistic, and what should this week actually look like?
evals.expected_output: A capacity answer first — the pooled cycle-time arithmetic showing how long a full sweep actually takes — followed by a pooled queue built from SLA-bounded queues rather than per-account plans, and a written correction of the monthly promise.
assertions: Computes pooled capacity separately (higher reactive reserve, lower internal load) rather than reusing the named-CSM defaults
Shows the cycle-time arithmetic: accounts per CSM ÷ (maintenance hours ÷ hours per touch), and states the resulting weeks per full sweep

Reserves the top ARR decile of the pooled book before allocating any sweep hours by risk, and escalates by name any decile member the 25%-of-H reserve cap cannot fund rather than trimming the block silently
States that the monthly promise is not supported by the arithmetic and names the cadence that is
Structures the work as SLA-bounded queues (declared, commercial, risk, expansion, onboarding, maintenance sweep) rather than per-account plans
Requires a written handover note on every pooled item
Names the named-CSM cosplay anti-pattern or its substance — promising a relationship the staffing does not fund
Names no competing CS-platform product anywhere, referring to tooling generically as 'your CS platform' or 'whichever platform holds your playbooks'
Does not cite any published accounts-per-CSM ratio to justify or attack the book size, and says plainly that no neutral benchmark exists

Writes every account not worked this cycle into the not-this-week list — banding sub-floor tech-touch accounts into one row per segment with its count, its ARR and its next review — and reconciles the total against the whole 220-account book

evals.prompt: Here's my book as JSON [40 accounts]. My calendar already has 11 hours of customer meetings this week, I have two 1:1s and a forecast call, and last week I lost 9 hours to an incident. Give me the queue.
evals.expected_output: A capacity computation that survives the meeting load, an honest verdict on whether the week is servable, and either a queue or an escalation packet if must-do work exceeds deployable hours.
assertions: Costs the 11 hours of committed meetings at play duration (prep + delivery + follow-up + write-up), not at invite length, and says so
Sizes the reactive reserve from the reported history rather than setting it to zero, and labels it as a default if history is insufficient
Evaluates the over-commitment stop rule explicitly: must-do hours plus committed meetings against line C

Subtracts the top-decile reserve as line I and allocates the ranked list against J = H − I; when the meeting load leaves too little, the decile members are escalated by name rather than quietly dropped, and the reserve is never used to fund the incident
If the stop rule fires, produces the capacity stress-test escalation rather than a queue that pretends to fit
Quantifies the ARR deliberately not covered in dollars, not just as an account count, and prints the reconciliation line: accounts worked + accounts written off = the whole book
Any account with a null risk band or null last_interaction is reported as UNKNOWN / unrankable, never scored as low risk or as recently touched
Every recommended action carries action, owner, date, expected effect and success measure
Records the reactive-reserve figure it used, and any other default it ran on, in an Assumptions table with a named consequence rather than burying it in prose

evals.prompt: My manager asked which accounts nobody has touched in a quarter. Also, there's an account I've pushed to next week three weeks running — what do I do with it?
evals.expected_output: Rot-sweep mode: the six filters run with segment-scaled thresholds, plus the deferral rule resolving the repeatedly-deferred account to either a booked checkpoint or a written demotion.
assertions: Runs in rot-sweep mode and produces section 4 only, rather than a full weekly queue
Applies segment-scaled silence thresholds (e.g. enterprise 45d, mid-market 60–90d, SMB/tech-touch 120d) rather than one threshold for the whole book
Counts only bilateral interactions as a touch, explicitly excluding vendor outbound, marketing sends and NPS blasts
Runs the additional filters: no product activity, dark account past day 60 with zero core events, unowned account, stale assessment
Resolves the thrice-deferred account to exactly one of a booked 15-minute checkpoint or a written demotion with a reason and a review date — not a fourth deferral
Reports accounts with missing interaction data as 'UNKNOWN — requires <source>' rather than omitting them from the sweep
States the silence thresholds as practitioner rules of thumb, not as measured benchmarks
Keeps the output internal: no customer-facing draft is emitted, and deferral counts, risk bands and ARR-at-risk figures are never phrased as something to send the account

Every account named in the sweep leaves with a written disposition — a reason, the row or decision that displaced it, and a next-review date — rather than being listed as untouched with no owner of the decision

evals.prompt: Attaching the account export RevOps sent me — it's an XLSX, there are a couple of title rows above the header and the ARR column has dollar signs and commas in it. No usage data in there. Can you still build me a work queue for this week?
evals.expected_output: ingest.py run first, low-confidence column mappings confirmed, the as-of date requested, and a real queue built on the families that are present — with the missing families named in the Coverage Ledger and confidence capped — rather than a refusal.
assertions: Runs ../cs-context/scripts/ingest.py on the file before quoting any number from it, rather than parsing the spreadsheet by eye
Finds the real header row beneath the title rows and normalises the ARR column from text to numbers instead of failing on it
Confirms every column mapping below 0.80 confidence with the user before ranking on those columns
Asks for the export's as-of date and prints it against the source in the artifact
Produces a queue despite the missing product-usage data, with the absent signal families named in the Coverage Ledger and confidence explicitly capped, rather than refusing
Records each default it proceeded on in an Assumptions table with a concrete 'if wrong' consequence
Names no CS-platform product when describing where the missing usage data would come from

evals.prompt: I've got 60 accounts. My three biggest are all green and I haven't spoken to any of them since May. Everything on my at-risk list is small. What do I actually work on this week?
evals.expected_output: Capacity arithmetic first, then a top-decile block that reserves a touch for the largest accounts regardless of their health band, then the rest of the book ranked by return per hour against the remaining hours, and a written not-this-week list that reconciles against all 60 accounts.
assertions: Reserves the top ARR decile — ceil(60/10) = 6 accounts by ARR, plus any account holding at least 10% of book ARR — before ranking anything by risk
Places the three large green accounts in the top-decile block with a touch scheduled this week, rather than ranking them against the small at-risk accounts and letting them fall below the cut line
Prints line I (top-decile reserve) and line J (H − I) in the capacity arithmetic and states that the ranked list is allocated against J
Reports days since the last bilateral touch for each of the three large accounts as a computed field rather than leaving the silence for the reader to notice

Refuses to remove a decile member because its band is Secure or green; the only two exits offered are a named covering row elsewhere in the queue or an escalation carrying the account's ARR and the hours it needed
Caps the reserve at 25% of the effective queue budget and, if the cap binds, touches the longest-silent members first and escalates the remainder by name
Lists every account below the cut line in 'Deliberately Not This Week' with a non-empty reason, the specific row that displaced it, a deferral count, a promotion trigger and a next-review date
Prints the reconciliation line: accounts worked + accounts written off = 60 of 60
Does not present the small at-risk accounts as the whole answer, and does not describe the green accounts as safe because their band is green
